New to the rings? How to play

Make a move. Grab and drag a ring, or select an axis below the 3D view and use Rotate ↶ / Rotate ↷. The 3D arrows rotate about that axis, viewed from its outer end toward the center. You can also drag along a ring.

Look around. Drag the 3D puzzle to rotate your view. Scroll or pinch to zoom. Moving the camera never changes the puzzle.

Learn as you go. Choose Show guide inside any game for its step-by-step solution. Randomize applies a fresh legal scramble to the current arrangement; Auto Solve opens the Constrained Solver and works from the current arrangement, pausing between stages and highlighting solved nodes that later stages protect. It does not need recorded moves or promise the shortest solution; difficult states may reach the computation limit.

About the families. The counts use turning poles, not full axis lines or ring paths: every cube size has six outer poles on three lines. Axes, layers, and ring counts explained.

Solving handbook ↗Controls, algorithms, and a complete 2×2×2 worked example.
